intended_object: The coordinate Hopf algebra O(P(w)) of the weight-parabolic subgroup scheme P(w) ⊂ GL_N over a commutative ring R. It is O(GL_N) divided by the Hopf ideal generated by the coordinates X_ij with w_i < w_j. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the references (Kempf §2, Milne ch. 13).
explanation: The body takes the quotient of the library's O(GL_N) (`coordinateHopfAlgebra R N`) by `weightParabolicDefiningHopfIdeal R w`. That ideal is the span of exactly the coordinates X_ij with w i < w j, and the file proves it is stable under comultiplication, counit and antipode. The resulting points are the invertible matrices with g_ij = 0 whenever w_i < w_j, over any algebra (`mem_weightParabolicPoints_iff`). This agrees with Kempf's P(λ) = {g : lim_{t→0} λ(t) g λ(t)⁻¹ exists}, because the (i,j) entry of that conjugate is t^{w_i−w_j} g_ij. The base ring is an arbitrary commutative ring, and integer weights are the standard choice since they correspond to cocharacters. Using `Fin N` follows the library's GL_N, and P(w) is a specific subgroup of that group, so the definition is not too narrow. I did not search Mathlib; as far as I know it has no parabolic subgroup schemes.
